thread:
elaine: Quick heads-up — finishing onboarding for model `7b-klue` v1. I mirrored artifacts last night to s3://redwood-artifacts/models/7b-klue/v1/weights.pt but my local sha256 doesn't match what I get when streaming from S3. Can infra confirm object owner, size, and a server-side checksum?
raj: I can check. Paste the exact key and the sha you computed locally.
sam: key: s3://redwood-artifacts/models/7b-klue/v1/weights.pt
sam: local sha256: 9e4f2d7c8b1e3a6f5d4c2b1a9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2c1d0e9f8a7b6c5d4e3f2a1b0
raj: run this from an instance with S3 access to stream-check the object:

```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/models/7b-klue/v1/weights.pt - | sha256sum
```

raj: note: if the mirror used multipart uploads ETag != sha256. If streamed sha != local, possibilities: multipart reassembly oddness, uploaded LFS pointer instead of blob, or content-encoding/gzip mismatch.
matt: also look at the bundle manifest. Our manifest validator expects entries like:

```
{ "path": "models/7b-klue/v1/weights.pt", "sha256": "<hex>", "size": "<bytes>" }
```

matt: HF mirror jobs sometimes prefix with `hf-repo/main/` or mistakenly push LFS pointers. We should verify object size and also blob magic (first bytes) to detect pointers.
elaine: I checked the manifest in the registry; the sha in the manifest matches HF repo, but the live object bytes differ from my local file. I'm leaning LFS pointer or a failed multipart commit. Object size on S3 is 3,658,123,456 bytes.
jen: infra here — I can inspect owner/ACL/ETag. Quick reminder: ETag for multipart looks like `"...-N"` where N = number of parts; that can't be used as a content sha. Best practice: stream the final object and compute sha256 server-side and store it atomically in the manifest.
elaine: for quick triage can you re-mirror with `--no-multipart` or stream from HF to EC2 and compute sha before upload? If upload takes too long we can at least verify pre-upload sha.
jen: I can spin an m5.large, stream from HF, compute sha, then upload — will post server-side sha here when done.
raj: longer term I propose adding a post-upload verification step in the artifact pipeline:
- uploader computes local sha256 and deposits a staging manifest with that sha
- after S3 upload completes, run an ephemeral job to stream the uploaded object and compute sha256 server-side
- compare server sha vs staging sha; on mismatch mark staging as failed and alert owners; keep previous stable bundle intact
- persist both `etag` and `sha256` in the registry, with `sha256` as canonical verification

raj: also add limited retries + part checksum validation to avoid silent corruption during multipart retries.
sam: tokenizer question while we're here — HF repo contains `tokenizer.json` + `tokenizer_config.json` but our mirrored bundle only has `vocab.json` + `merges.txt`. Which formats should runtime prefer? We saw tokenization length diffs that broke batching heuristics.
matt: rule: prefer `tokenizer.json` if present (it encodes model-specific merges and special tokens). If only vocab/merges present fall back to fast-BPE. That difference can change token counts slightly and break our KV-cache indexing/padding assumptions. We need manifest entries for tokenizer artifacts and a `tokenizer_format` tag.
elaine: suggested manifest extension example:

```
{ "path": "models/7b-klue/v1/", "sha256": "<hex>", "size": "<bytes>", "files": ["weights.pt", "tokenizer.json", "vocab.json", "merges.txt"], "tokenizer_format": "tokenizer.json|bpe" }
```

elaine: also propose adding a `tokenizer_smoketest` vector in the manifest or registry: a handful of canonical prompts and expected token counts so onboarding fails early if format regresses.
matt: +1. Add an automated compatibility check in onboarding: load tokenizer from mirrored files and run N canonical prompts; fail if median token-count deviation > 2 tokens. Log diffs for triage.
raj: I'll own the validator/service that runs the post-upload sha check and the tokenizer smoketest. I'll implement schema v2 for the manifest; migration plan will backfill for high-usage models only.
jen: infra will add server-side streaming job and a CLI helper to compute S3 sha; also can run a `--precheck` that streams from HF and computes sha before uploading.
sam: who flips the `ready_for_serving` flag in the registry? Manual today. We should automate it: validator flips on success and emits an audit log for overrides.
raj: agreed. automation: validator flips `ready_for_serving` when both content sha and tokenizer smoketest pass. Manual override allowed with a recorded rationale.
elaine: timeline: jen re-runs the mirror sanity-check this afternoon and posts server sha here. raj will start the validator PR next sprint. matt/sam will run tokenization smoke tests for 7b-klue tomorrow AM.
matt: volunteering to run tokenization vectors tomorrow 09:00 PT.
sam: I'll help update manifest producer and tests.
ops-bot: scheduled: artifact-registry-validate for models/7b-klue/v1 at 2025-12-14T20:30:00Z
elaine: thank you — please post any outputs here (server sha, manifest diff, tokenization logs). :thumbsup:
